newsitem.title: UK: Agency co-operation on Sumitomo very effective - LME.
newsitem.headline: Agency co-operation on Sumitomo very effective - LME.

text.p: International co-operation over the Sumitomo Corp scandal between the London Metal Exchange (LME) and British and U.S. regulators was very effective, the LME said in a letter to chairman of the U.S. House Banking Committee.

"It is the LME's belief that when the full facts of the Sumitomo affair become known, it will be shown that the international co-operation which existed between the LME, the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) and the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) in the U.K. and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in the U.S. against the background of very difficult circumstances will be shown to have been very effective," LME chief executive David King wrote in the letter.

Memoranda of Understanding exist between the CFTC and NFA in the U.S. and SIB and the SFA in the U.K., and King said "the LME has and will co-operate fully with any appropriate authority within legal constaints and through appropriate channels."

In his letter King explained how the LME operates, adding that as with all markets which have derivatives, exchange contracts are only part of the cash market involving the actual physical metal moving in commercial channels.
If LME prices moved away from the cash market arbitrage would bring them back together.
"Additionally, it is believed that there is probably as much over-the-counter (OTC) metals trading taking place as there is on-Exchange trading," he added.

"The LME has neither information about nor jurisdiction over either OTC business or the underlying cash market. This is a difficulty experienced by most futures markets and one we would wish to address over time," King stated.
King said the LME would be happy to meet with the committee chairman and to discuss any questions the committee may have.
